Retrieved 3 March 2024. | capacity = 20,560{{Cite web|url=https://stadyumlar.net/eryaman-stadi/|title = Eryaman Stadı - Türkiye Stadyumları ve Stadyum Projeleri|date = 31 May 2019}} | coordinates = {{Coord|39.980278|32.613889|format=dms|type:landmark_scale:3000_region:TR|display=it}} | chrtitle = President | chairman = Arda Çakmak{{Cite web |date=2025-12-07 |title=Gençlerbirliği'nin yeni başkanı Arda Çakmak'tan Volkan Demirel açıklaması - Fanatik Gazetesi Futbol Haberleri - Spor |url=https://www.fanatik.com.tr/genclerbirligi/genclerbirliginin-yeni-baskani-arda-cakmaktan-volkan-demirel-aciklamasi-2603860 |access-date=2025-12-07 |website=Fanatik |language=tr}} | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Bernd Storck]] | league = {{Turkish football updater|Gençlerbirliği}} | season = {{Turkish football updater|Gençlerbirliği2}} | position = {{Turkish football updater|Gençlerbirliği3}} | website = {{URL|http://www.genclerbirligi.org.tr/}} | current = | pattern_b1 = _genclerbieligi2021h | pattern_la1 = _genclerbieligi2021h | pattern_ra1 = _genclerbieligi2021h | leftarm1 = 000000 | body1 = 000000 | rightarm1 = 000000 | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = 000000 | pattern_la2 = _thinredborder | pattern_b2 = _nike_white | pattern_ra2 = _thinredborder | pattern_sh2 = _nikered | pattern_so2 = _nikered | leftarm2 = 000000 | body2 = 000000 | rightarm2 = 000000 | shorts2 = 000000 | socks2 = 000000 | pattern_la3 = _thinredborder | pattern_b3 = _nike_white | pattern_ra3 = _thinredborder | pattern_sh3 = _nikered | pattern_so3 = _nikered | leftarm3 = 40E0D0 | body3 = 40E0D0 | rightarm3 = 40E0D0 | shorts3 = 40E0D0 | socks3 = 40E0D0 }} '''Gençlerbirliği Spor Kulübü''' (pronounced {{IPA|tr|ɟentʃˈlæɾbiɾli.i}}), commonly known as '''Gençlerbirliği''', is a multi-sport organisation from [[Ankara]] best known for its men's professional football team, which currently competes in the [[Süper Lig]] and hosts matches at the 20,560-seat [[Eryaman Stadium]] on the city's western edge. Founded on 14 March 1923 by pupils of Ankara Erkek Lisesi who were excluded from their school side, the club soon became a symbol of youthful rebellion and has been nicknamed '''Ankara Rüzgârı''' ''("Wind of Ankara")'' and '''Gençler''' ''("The Youth")'' ever since. Its traditional colours are red and black, chosen—according to club lore—either because those were the only fabrics available at a local tailor or because they echo the red-and-black poppies that flower on the Anatolian steppe each spring. Historically, Gençlerbirliği were a dominant force in the regional [[Ankara Football League]], winning that competition a record nine times before the nationwide league system was introduced in 1959. National silverware followed: the club captured the [[Turkish Football Championship]] twice, in 1941 and 1946, and lifted the [[Turkish Cup]] in both 1987 and 2001; the latter triumph earned a memorable [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]] run in [[2003–04 UEFA Cup|2003–04]] in which the side eliminated [[Blackburn Rovers F.C.|Blackburn Rovers]], [[Sporting CP]] and [[Parma Calcio 1913|Parma]] before bowing out to eventual champions [[Valencia CF|Valencia]] in the fourth round. League highlights include third-place finishes in 1965–66 and 2002–03, the latter season under manager [[Ersun Yanal]] producing the highest points total in club history. Gençlerbirliği are also renowned for an academy and scouting network that has developed internationals such as [[Geremi]], [[Isaac Promise]] and [[Arda Güler]]. The club's main rivalry is with fellow [[Ankara]] side [[MKE Ankaragücü|Ankaragücü]]; their meetings are dubbed the '''Ankara derby''' and are among the oldest continuously played local derbies in [[Football in Turkey|Turkish football]]. Off the pitch, Gençlerbirliği have long been associated with pragmatic financial management—initiated by legendary president [[İlhan Cavcav]]—as well as a politically active supporter base known for choreographed tifos and social-justice campaigns."}}
